correctness.rationale: The first-force argument in the cubic graph reduces every candidate four-set to one closed neighborhood plus one extra vertex. A complete modular-neighborhood check gives exactly four allowed positions for that extra vertex; each allowed position creates two consecutive full antipodal rungs and hence a deterministic propagation around the ladder. The rooted cases reduce to five disjoint dihedral orbits, whose stabilizer sizes give total \(13n\). The \(n=3\) boundary is independently handled as \(K_{3,3}\). The packaged exhaustive checker confirms the criterion and orbit census through order \(24\).

value.rationale: The Möbius ladder is a standard cubic circulant with a long-known scalar zero forcing number. Classifying every optimal initial set is a natural refinement: it gives the leading coefficient of the zero forcing polynomial and a symmetry-resolved description of optimal configurations. This is a complete structural result on an infinite named family, not a routine recomputation of the scalar minimum.
